messages:
ranjit: heads up — noticed a sharp p95 east-west latency jump across gpu nodes during the 11:38-11:50 batching window. pods hit retries and some batches requeued.
sarah: saw that too, ~30-60ms spikes, usually <3ms. affected racks: rack-5 and rack-12 mostly.
mike: any packet loss numbers? TCP retransmits?
ranjit: tcp retransmits spike ~0.6-1% on those flows, icmp mtr shows intermittent 1-2% packet loss between node-5b -> node-12c, path alternates (ECMP) across two TORs.
jessica: could this be MTU/fragmentation? last week we toggled jumbo autoneg on a subset during a firmware upgrade.
netops-bot: deploy-notice: TOR firmware 2026.03.11 pushed to rack-12 (partial) at 2026-03-11T02:45Z.
sarah: okay that matches timeline — some racks got updated earlier than others. ranjit can you paste one of the flow traces?
ranjit: paste: ```
mtr -r -c 50 node-5b node-12c

Host             Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
node-5b            0.0%    50    0.3   0.7   0.2  30.1  5.4
tor-5              0.0%    50    0.4   0.9   0.3  35.2  6.8
core-agg           0.0%    50    1.2   1.6   0.8  20.8  3.9
tor-12             1.8%    50   28.1  29.7  18.6  59.9  9.0
node-12c           0.0%    50    0.8   1.2   0.4  15.3  2.9
```
ranjit: note the big variance when hitting tor-12 hop.
mike: that looks asymmetric — flows are sometimes routed via an alternate TOR where MTU is 1500 vs 9000. fragmentation/encap on the smaller MTU path could explain the higher latency. can you run `ethtool -k` and `ip link` on node-12c and node-5b?
sarah: also run `ibstat -p` / `rdma_pingpong` to confirm if RDMA fell back. RDMA fallback to TCP would inflate latency massively for token-serving bursts.
jessica: running quick checks now.
jessica: node-12c `ip link show` shows mtu 1500 on bond0, but node-12c was supposed to have 9000. tor-12 reports mtu 1500 on the uplink after fw push.
jessica: `ethtool -S` shows TX queue err counters tick during the window, small bursts of OFLD/segmentation on the 25g link.
ranjit: so partial firmware rollout created inconsistent MTU state across fabric, ECMP made flows alternate path with different MTUs -> some packets fragmented/encapped -> bigger transmission latency during peak bursts.
mike: that fits. mitigation options: 1) rollback TOR fw on rack-12, 2) pin batch-critical nodes to single path via policy routing or OVS flow pinning, 3) temporarily lower batch sizes to reduce amplification.
sarah: can we quick pin the hot nodes to dedicated segment? netops, can you add a 5-minute flow pin rule for pods with label `batch-window=hot`?
jessica: I can push a BGP MED-based preference to avoid tor-12 for those flows for the next 30m. doing that now.
netops-bot: change-request: announced route preference update for prefix 10.40.120.0/24 (rack-5 hot pool) applied.
ranjit: after the MED change p95 dropped back to ~4ms in the next batch window. monitoring continues.
mike: still want rollback for tor-12 fw until we validate jumbo handling on all TORs. can infra-sre schedule rollback?
sarah: +1, opening rollback ticket and scheduling for next maintenance window.
jessica: adding postmortem note: partial TOR firmware rollout caused MTU mismatch -> ECMP path asymmetry -> fragmentation and RDMA/TCP fallback spikes during high-concurrency batching. short-term mitigations: route preference pin + reduced batch sizes. long-term: stricter preflight for fw that touches MTU/encap, and fabric canary on a micro-rack before fleet rollout.
ranjit: filing the incident doc with graphs and commands used. thanks team, will follow up with perf numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
